analysis.title: Turning the Page on Last Week (John Flood, GS FICC & Equities, 9 Nov 2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 implied move through Friday is 2.29%. CPI is the macro focus tomorrow, with GIR at +16bps for core MoM.
Last Friday's jobs print was +165k vs ~65k expected. It calmed the growth scare narrative but pushed December hike odds above 80%.

GS clients have net sold $30b of tech stocks (TMT + Comm Services) on the U.S. trading desk since the start of October, $6b of it last week. During July's momentum drawdown clients net sold $23b of tech.
Friday 11/6 was the first day in 7 trading sessions that the GS desk ended with a buy skew in tech (+$1b).

Investors are recalibrating datacenter build expectations after last week's midterm elections, especially in TX and OH. Feedback is that market prices imply limited y/y capex (or GW) growth in 2028, well below prior expectations of 30-40%+ y/y growth. Many clients see that as an attractive entry point, and the author shares this view.
PB data through 11/5: US Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 pts, the largest weekly decline since March 2020, to 207.5% (26th percentile one-year).
US Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.7 pts, the largest weekly decline since the week of Liberation Day (April 2025), to 43.3% (0th percentile five-year).
Performance through 11/6: US Fundamental L/S HFs lost 50bps last week (+6% ytd). Global Systematics lost 150bps (+14.8% ytd).

Five PB book sleeves stand out: Mag 7/Hyperscalers (net allocation near record highs), Housing/Homebuilders (net short, L/S ratio at 5-year lows), Restaurants (L/S ratio at 5-year lows), Power/US Electrical Equipment (net short, L/S ratio at 5-year lows), SMID Biotech (net long, L/S ratio above 3 but near 3-year lows).

Author's reasons to stay constructive: S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth tracking at 35% y/y (excluding mega-cap tech 'other income'), market breadth improving sharply, S&P 500 P/E valuations cheap relative to history, and corporates buying the dip.
